_description: Material-function technique extracted from /Game/VFX/NiagaraDissolveEdge/Materials/MaterialFunction/MF_DissolveEdge. Use this as a reusable threshold-mask block for dissolve edges, erosion cutoffs, binary reveal bands, and Niagara/material sync masks.
overview: This function is intentionally simple. It takes a scalar texture or noise input, clamps it to a safe 0-1 range, compares it against a scalar threshold amount, and returns a binary mask. Its value is not visual richness by itself. Its value is being a clean reusable decision block inside larger dissolve or edge-authoring graphs.

inputs.name: Texture
inputs.role: The grayscale source field to threshold. Usually a noise sample, dissolve texture channel, or other scalar mask.

inputs.name: Amount
inputs.role: The threshold or dissolve amount. Higher values reveal/keep less of the source depending on how the caller interprets the returned mask.

outputs.name: Mask
outputs.role: A clean binary 0/1 mask derived from the threshold comparison.

internal_logic: Clamp the incoming scalar texture/mask to the 0-1 range.
Compare the clamped value against the Amount input using an If node.
Return the result as the dissolve/reveal mask.

practical_meaning.behavior: The function returns 1 when the source value is less than or equal to the threshold, and 0 when the source value is above the threshold.
practical_meaning.artist_read: Think of this as a hard cutoff: everything under the threshold survives, everything over the threshold is removed.
practical_meaning.visual_role: This is the hard binary stage in a dissolve graph. Edge glow, softness, emissive border, and secondary breakup must be layered outside this function.

best_use_cases: basic dissolve cutoff from a grayscale noise texture
erosion threshold mask before edge-emissive extraction
binary reveal mask for portal or summoning transitions
material-side mask that should stay in sync with a Niagara threshold parameter
simple kill/reveal logic before adding a soft edge band
not_for: final portal ring shaping by itself
full hero dissolve look without extra edge logic
continuous grayscale fade where a hard threshold is not desired

use_before: Subtracting a wider and narrower threshold result to isolate an edge band
Multiplying the mask into opacity or opacity mask
Driving emissive edge logic with a separate border calculation
pair_with: fresnel or radial gradient edge shaping
a second offset threshold for edge-band extraction
Niagara user parameter or dynamic parameter for synchronized dissolve progress
avoid: using this function as the only dissolve logic in a hero graph
expecting this function to provide soft falloff by itself
burying its threshold amount so artists cannot tune it

agent_recipe.step_1: Sample or compute a scalar field that represents dissolve/noise intensity.
agent_recipe.step_2: Feed that scalar field into MF_DissolveEdge as the Texture input.
agent_recipe.step_3: Feed the reveal threshold or dissolve progress into the Amount input.
agent_recipe.step_4: Use the returned Mask as the hard binary cutoff for opacity or for further edge extraction logic.
agent_recipe.step_5: If an emissive edge is needed, generate a second threshold at a nearby amount and subtract the two masks to get a narrow border band.
agent_recipe.step_6: Expose the threshold-driving amount as an artist-facing or system-driven parameter.

niagara_integration_notes: This function is a good match for Niagara-driven dissolve because Niagara can drive the same Amount value used in the material.
Use the same normalized parameter naming on both sides when possible, such as DissolveAmount or TransformAlpha.
If particles should emit from the dissolve edge, derive a narrow edge band in the material and mirror the same threshold logic in Niagara spawn logic.
common_failure_modes: Calling material has no secondary edge band, so the dissolve looks too binary and cheap.
Amount is not exposed, so the function is technically reusable but not artist-friendly.
The source texture is not normalized or clamped, causing unstable threshold behavior.
The team expects soft falloff from a function that is intentionally a hard cutoff.
key_takeaway: MF_DissolveEdge is valuable because it is small, stable, and clear. ForgePilot should learn it as a threshold-mask building block, not mistake it for a complete dissolve look.
